text: #294's step 6 (#359): the gate proves selected Python functions in place. verify.Check and verify.Run admit a check that selects an in-place proof beside conformance on the same function; the direct Python check refuses it, since it returns no proof. Before anything runs, the gate builds every selected function's verifier input, refusing a selection the input can't preserve. After the application's tests, conformance and backing tests, it runs the pinned Nagini from its recipe on each input, apart from the application's image, records each attempt in the application report and attributes its result as component proof evidence. A selected proof qualifies only as an effective guarantee: the function proved from its original bytes, with no error and nothing it reached unaccounted for, every trusted contract it assumed tested, and conformance on the same function passing in the same session against the same source bytes, since the gate's collector binds what conformance observes to that very staged declaration. A selected proof that doesn't qualify fails the gate, as an untested declared contract does, and every other kind of evidence stays as it was. Receipts show each proof as holding only on the condition that its named trusted contracts hold, which tests support and nothing proves, list the verifier input's spans, how it binds each name and what it leaves out, and name each shortfall among the failures; fingerprints bind each attempt's input, recipe and result, never its local image, command or Nagini's output. A proof covers only the selected function's own body: no dependency, no unselected function and not the whole application.
